name: Later
summary: Visual social media scheduler and planner. Plan, preview and auto-publish posts across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and more from one calendar.
best_for: creators and visual-first brands (Instagram/TikTok-centric) that want drag-and-drop visual planning, link-in-bio and scheduling in one
skip_if: you need deep multi-network publishing, listening and team workflows at agency scale (suite-class tools fit), or the post caps chafe immediately
honest_knock: The Starter caps are where the price really lives: 30 posts per profile and 3 months of analytics run out fast for an active brand, pushing real users toward Growth — so compare at the tier you'll actually need, not the entry price. Later's visual-first planning (born from Instagram) is still its strength; if your world is link-in-bio commerce and grids, that focus earns its seat.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-17 and 2026-10-07) Starter $18.75/month, Growth $37.50 and Scale $82.50, all billed yearly, which Later advertises as three months free and 25% off against monthly. Every plan opens with a 14-day trial, and on the page as we read it on 31 August 2026 that trial is the only no-cost route offered: three paid tiers, nothing beneath them, and an FAQ that discusses users per plan rather than any zero-price option. Our earlier note here also described a permanently free option, which we could not source; Later has historically run a no-cost link-in-bio product that may still sit behind the signup flow, but the pricing page does not sell it. Included per plan: Starter 1 Social Set (one profile on each of eight networks), 1 user, 30 posts per profile a month and 5 AI credits; Growth 2 sets, 2 users, 180 posts and 50 credits; Scale 6 sets, 4 users, unlimited posts and 100 credits. Add-ons are sold on Growth and Scale only; the Starter card says extra Social Sets, users and AI credits are not available. On Growth and Scale extra Social Sets are $11.25 a month each, extra users $3.75 a month each, and extra AI credits $3.75 a month per 100 credits. Starter covers casual scheduling; Growth adds the inbox, approvals and longer analytics; Scale is aimed at enterprise-level analytics without an enterprise contract.
